summary: Bhadriraju Krishnamurti was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Pennsylvania under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He held posts at Andhra University, UC Berkeley, Osmania University (where he was professor and founder), and the University of Hyderabad.

Bhagavan Das was an Indologist and philosopher who earned an M.A. from the University of Calcutta. He co-founded Banaras Hindu University, served at Central Hindu College, and was headmaster at the Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith, which he also founded.

Bhagirath Prasad Tripathi is an Indology and linguistics scholar. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, where he is attested in 1976 and served as head of the Research Department in 1989.

Bhagwan Dash was a scholar in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda, Tribhuvan University, and the University of Delhi, and later served as a bibliographer and cataloguer at the Library of Congress.

Bhagwanlal Indraji worked in Indology and history/archaeology, receiving an honorary doctorate from Leiden University in 1884. He held memberships in the Royal Asiatic Society and the Asiatic Society of Mumbai, and was a Fellow at the University of Mumbai.

Bhajagobinda Ghosh worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. In 1994, he was attested as an editorial board member of the Bulletin of Tibetology and as assistant director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

Bharat Bhushan Vidyalankar works in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, the University of Delhi, and Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University, Agra, and held posts at Kendriya Hindi Sansthan and Sandhaan.

Bharat Gupt is an Indologist who studied at the University of Toronto, the University of Delhi, and Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda. He held a post as associate professor at the University of Delhi (attested 1999).

Bhaskar Anand Saletore was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who studied under Henry Heras and doctoral supervisor Lionel David Barnett. In 1936, he served as Professor of History at Sir Parashurambhau College.
Bhau Daji worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his studies at Elphinstone College and Grant Medical College and Sir Jamshedjee Jeejeebhoy Group of Hospitals around 1845–1851.
Bhesh Narayan Dahal works in Indology and history/archaeology. In 2018, he held posts at the National Archives of Nepal and served as an editorial board member for Documenta Nepalica.

Bhikkhu Anālayo is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Peradeniya and University of Marburg, and held posts at the University of Hamburg, Sri Lanka International Buddhist Academy, and Barre Center for Buddhist Studies.

Bhikkhu Bodhi is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Brooklyn College and Claremont Graduate University, and trained under Nyanaponika Thera. He served as editor at the Buddhist Publication Society and president of the Buddhist Association of the United States.

Bhikkhu Pāsādika works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, having studied at Magadh University and Punjabi University. His posts include positions at Punjabi University, the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the University of Marburg.
Bhikkhu U Dhammissara is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, studying under supervisor Sanu Mahatthanadull (attested 2017).

Bhikkhuni Dhammanandā is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She completed a Doctor of Philosophy at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2007), studying under doctoral supervisors Tilak Kariyawasam and Daya Edirisinghe.

Bhikkhunī Dhammadinnā is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She held posts at the Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts (attested 2012–2022), the University of Marburg (attested 2020), and Dharmamitra (attested 2026).

Bhogilal Sandesara was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh. He served as Head of the Gujarati Department at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda and as Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (~1958–1975).

Bhuwan Lal Joshi was an Indologist who studied at Patna University from approximately 1952 to 1954. He held academic posts at the University of California, Berkeley (~1962–1967) and the University of California, Santa Cruz (~1967–1977).

Bidia Dandaron was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Andrei Vostrikov. He held research posts at the Buryat Institute of Social Sciences and the Institute of Mongolian, Buddhist and Tibetan Studies.
